sources.entry: Rocket.Chat - Communications platform that puts data protection first (alternative to Gitter.im and Slack). (Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: Rocket.Chat is an open-source, self-hostable team communications platform written in TypeScript, offering real-time chat, voice calls, federation, and end-to-end encryption.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Rocket.Chat as a team communications platform for real-time conversations between colleagues, with other companies, and with customers. It can be deployed self-hosted (Docker, Podman, or Kubernetes), via Launchpad for a Kubernetes setup, in an air-gapped network, or as a premium cloud-hosted service. Stated features include messaging, voice calls, federation across a federated network, end-to-end encryption, identity management, and role and attribute-based access control. It has desktop apps (Mac App Store, Windows Store, Snapcraft) and a mobile app, and supports public apps from a Marketplace plus custom apps built with the open-source Apps-Engine. The README also links to user, admin, developer, and API documentation, plus a Trust Center and Compliance Center.
use_cases: customer communication with a chat widget or omnichannel
building custom chat integrations and apps
how_to_run: Deploy with Docker, Podman, or Kubernetes (see the Deployment Guide in the docs)
Or use Launchpad for a quick Kubernetes setup
Desktop app: sudo snap install rocketchat-desktop (Linux)
Developers: follow the server development environment guides for Linux, Windows, Mac, or Gitpod
notable: Federation support for communicating across a federated network
Air-gapped deployment option without internet access
Apps-Engine and a Marketplace for extending the platform
End-to-end encryption with role and attribute-based access control
Official desktop apps for Mac, Windows, and Linux (Snap)
caveats: Some deployment options, such as dedicated cloud hosting, are premium paid offerings
System requirements must be checked before deploying a workspace
Desktop and mobile apps are separate repositories and installers
